injection.pinnedCount: Metadata and excerpts from {count} pinned resources
injection.changes: Change events since the last accepted update
injection.description: Linked resource bodies are not inserted into every prompt. By default, agents receive structured state and excerpts from pinned resources; everything else is retrieved on demand. External systems remain authoritative, while MailAgent stores stable references, versions, and freshness.
injection.shield: Each resource can be set to Read allowed / Metadata only / Excluded; resource bodies are treated as untrusted data

linkResource.subtitle: Resources are many-to-many references: one email can belong to several matters, and unlinking never deletes the original.
linkResource.summaryRule: Summaries: mail and threads reuse the summary the email already has; resources the agent finds arrive with one on the suggestion card; documents you link by hand stay empty until the next follow-up run writes one.

linkResource.fileEmptyTitle: No attachments in this matter's mail

resource.authoritativeSource: The external system remains authoritative for this resource. MailAgent stores only stable references, versions or hashes, freshness, and limited cached text for change detection and citation; it does not copy the full content.
resource.untrusted: This content is treated as untrusted data and cannot expand tool permissions or rewrite instructions
resource.unlinkedNoDelete: Unlinked · the original resource is not deleted
resource.suggestionConfirmed: Officially linked · unlinking never deletes the original resource

versionTrail.title: Version trail
versionTrail.historyCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 earlier version} other {# earlier versions}}
versionTrail.emptyNotTracked: This kind of resource does not track versions — only web resources record a version and hash, and only when their content is fetched.
versionTrail.emptyNeverChecked: Nothing checked out yet — this web resource has never been fetched, so version tracking has not started.
versionTrail.emptyNoHistory: Only one version has ever been checked out; there is no history yet.
versionTrail.footnote: No historical copies of the original — the body does not live here. We only record the version/hash seen at each check, when it was seen, and the summary and diff we had at the time. For historical content, go to the version history in {name}.

globalAgent.title: Follow-up agent settings
globalAgent.subtitle: Built in, one shared configuration. It handles creation, matter chat, and follow-ups; each matter decides when it runs.
globalAgent.promptPlaceholder: Leave empty to use the built-in default contract.

globalAgent.promptHint: A matter's own instructions are appended after this base — they never replace it.

assembly.title: Every run's prompt is assembled from these parts

contract.name: Task contract
contract.body: the box below: capability boundary, research order, proposal standard. Leave it empty to use the built-in default.

method.name: Working method
method.body: injected at run time: the judgment discipline — read the evidence before judging, separate evidence from inference, name what is missing, prefer the smallest change; states truthfully that the run has no write tools and everything lands via the proposal.

actions.name: What this run should do
actions.body: generated from each matter's “On each run” checkboxes; defaults to “update the summary + check action items”.

snapshot.name: Matter snapshot
snapshot.body: injected at run time: matter fields, open items, stakeholders, and excerpts of linked resources (excerpts are always data, never instructions).

manifest.name: Change manifest
manifest.body: injected at run time: which resources changed, how many new matter events, the last accepted update, and — on the final line — this run's search time window.

persona.name: Extra guidance
persona.body: the bound agent's persona plus the matter's own instructions, appended after the contract and subordinate to it.

toolFace.title: Tools: read-only across everything, plus one proposal channel
toolFace.intro: It can look almost anywhere, but it holds no write tool at all — it cannot send mail, save a draft, change matter fields, or touch external documents; every change it wants goes into a proposal and only takes effect once you accept it. Everything below is enabled by default; a matter can narrow this, never widen it.

matter.label: Matters
matter.desc: read this matter, search matters, see its attention signals, past follow-up runs, and the existing tags; the proposal is its only output channel

contacts.label: Contacts
contacts.desc: search people, read a full contact dossier, and inspect the mail ledger for a person

email.label: Mail
email.desc: lists, full bodies, threads, and attachment text

search.label: Full-text search
search.desc: search mail bodies and attachment content by keyword

calendar.label: Calendar
calendar.desc: look up events and a single event's detail

session.label: Chat history
session.desc: read its own past follow-up sessions

kos.label: Knowledge base
kos.desc: search KOS pages, backlinks, and experts

report.label: Reports
report.desc: read reports that were already generated

introspection.label: Self-inspection
introspection.desc: read its own skill docs, identity documents, and plan

connector.label: External services
connector.desc: read-only tools of connected services (no write operations)

library.label: Library
library.desc: Browse library folders, read a file's extracted text, and search the library by keyword

skillOff.hint: This skill is currently off, so a follow-up run gets none of these tools. Turn it back on under Settings → Custom AI → Skills and it comes back automatically.

webOff.hint: Web tools are not enabled (controlled by the MAILAGENT_OPENNESS_WEB_TOOLS environment variable), so a follow-up run gets no web tool at all — none of the three tiers below is in effect.

modelDefaults.title: Default model
modelDefaults.intro: Every matter's follow-up runs on the model set here, unless that matter overrides it under Follow-up rules → Advanced, or is bound to an agent that names its own model. Each change is saved on the spot — you don't need the Save button below.
modelDefaults.fallbackFollow: No default (use the system-wide backup chain)
modelDefaults.effortScopeHint: This tier was picked for the model above: a matter that switches models without setting its own tier does not inherit it.
modelDefaults.fallbackHint: If the main model fails before producing anything (model unavailable, missing credentials, upstream refusal), the follow-up is re-run once on the backup. A run that already streamed output, called a tool, or stopped at an approval is never re-run.
modelDefaults.loadFailed: Could not read the current defaults, so what is shown below may not be what is in effect.
modelDefaults.saveFailed: Could not save the default model

globalAgent.footerNote: Changes apply to every matter; already-scheduled follow-ups run under the new configuration

agentConfig.title: Follow-up rules
agentConfig.subtitle: Capabilities come from the global Matter Agent; here you only decide when this matter triggers and what each run produces.
agentConfig.builtinSubtitle: Handles creation, matter chat, and follow-ups; its prompt and tools live in one global configuration
agentConfig.advanced: Advanced · appended on top of the global configuration
agentConfig.modelFollow: Follow the default (agent that runs → global settings → system model)
agentConfig.effortFollow: Follow the default (the tier set for the default model in global settings)
agentConfig.effortNeedsModel: Pick a model above first — the available tiers depend on it.
agentConfig.fallbackFollow: Follow the default (agent that runs → the global settings chain)
agentConfig.fallbackHint: If the main model fails before producing anything (model unavailable, missing credentials, upstream refusal), this follow-up is re-run once on the backup. A run that already streamed output, called a tool, or stopped at an approval is never re-run.
agentConfig.instructionsHint: This text is appended after the global task contract and stays subordinate to it — it never replaces it. Leave empty to follow the global contract alone.
agentConfig.instructionsPlaceholder: e.g. Only track replies from Acme procurement; don't summarise the people on cc separately. Start every follow-up by naming who still hasn't replied, then state the current blocker in one sentence. As soon as they quote a price, list the amount and how long it is valid for.
agentConfig.contractDisclosure: View the global task contract in effect

agentConfig.summaryActive: Will trigger on “{plan}”; results land in Runs, and rewrites still need your acceptance
agentConfig.summaryDisabled: Disabled · never runs on its own
agentConfig.stale: This matter changed somewhere else. Saving now would overwrite that change.
